main_text.p: fic. Τπρεῖν ἢ χὴ, inquit, ἐωΰλον ὅτι μάλισα, μὴ πολλὰ φαίνονζ τῇ τὰ σώματ ἀ μερίων. Apud Hebraeos vox ערוה quae nuditatem significat, interdum etiam partes eas corporis notat quae neque oftendi neque nominari honeste possunt. An igitur & plebs Attica sic locuta? Nam haec quidem lectio in qua omnes mss. consentiunt manifesto ἐςράιζει.

Pag. 14. καὶ προαιρῶν δέ τι.] Signatum verbum προαιρεῖν, è pinn aliquid promere. Aristophanes Thesmophoriazusis —λῶ ἡμῖν πρὸ τὰ αὐτὰς ζαμιεῖς προαιρεῖσας λαβεῖν ἀλφιτον, ἔλαιον, οἶνον. est & apud Thucydidem in octaua προαιρεῖν pro ex horreo promere, siue deripere horreo, vt loquitur Horatius. Clemens Alex. προκομίζειν ἐν τῇ ζαμιείᾳ. Male autem vulgò scribitur προαιρῶν: quod manifestissimè declarant illa Diogenis Laertii in Lacyde, ἐπιδὰν γάρ τι προίληται τῆ ζαμιείᾳ. Saepe in hac voce peccatum offendes à librariis: saepe ab interpretibus. Sic in Lyside Platonis ἀσπαγάλυς ἐν τῷ φορμίσκῳ προαιρεῖσθαι, est, promere & educere, non autem feligere: vt vertunt. δῆμος φυγεῖν.] Fortasse δῆμος scribendum.

καὶ ζωρότερον οἶνον.] Vertimus meracium, neque tamen nos fugit quàm variae fuerint veterum criticorum sententiae super illo Homeri Ζωρότερον ἢ κέρασαι. vide grammaticos & Plutarchi Symposiaca. Aristotelem vero si sequimur auctorem in libro De poetica, vertemus auidius. page.notes: Greek and Hebrew readings are uncertain in several places: the first word of the page ("Τπρεῖν"), "ἐωΰλον", "ἀσπαγάλυς", "ἐπιδὰν", "προίληται" and the Hebrew "ערוה" were read from a small, low-contrast scan and should be checked against the original. The commentary block is set in smaller type inside the column, so it is marked as a foot paragraph. The word "antiqua" is split at the line end as "an-" and "tiqua"; the second part is recorded as the catchword.
